strings: m_c missed a tick while grooming, and is now suffering the consequences. {PRONOUN/m_c/subject/CAP} {VERB/m_c/have/has} tick fever.
Even if {PRONOUN/m_c/subject} can't find the exact bug responsible, m_c's new rash and fever clearly point to tick-borne illness.
Rash, fever, bad headache, all following a tick bite? It looks like m_c has tick fever.
Most tick bites are harmless. Most. m_c has tick fever.
It's tick season! c_n is fastidious in removing any parasites, but these bugs are sneaky, and it only takes one bad tick to infect m_c with tick fever.
Tick fever is almost never fatal. But m_c can't help but find that a bit hard to believe, shivering miserably with fever and headache in the most secluded corner of camp.
m_c is sick with tick fever.
After a tick bite becomes a fever and rash, m_c goes to the medicine den, where r_c0 diagnoses {PRONOUN/m_c/object} with tick fever.
After diagnosing m_c with tick fever, r_c0 instructs every Clanmate to check themselves for bites. One infected bug often means more.
High fever, pounding headache, full-body rash; though r_c0 insists tick fever is rarely fatal, m_c feels about halfway dead.
r_c0 searches the herb stores. m_c's newly diagnosed tick fever is rarely serious, but goldenrod and mullein are best for hastening recovery.
Shivering with fever and headache as {PRONOUN/m_c/subject} {VERB/m_c/choke/chokes} down r_c0's foul herb paste, m_c marvels at how a tiny tick bite could cause such awful sickness.
Aha! r_c0 plucks the tick from m_c's skin with a triumphant mrrow. Unfortunately, neither cat would have thought to look for the sneaky bug if m_c didn't already have a fever and rash.
Most tick bites are harmless. Most. r_c0 assures m_c tick fever is a very mild disease, but it's cold comfort.
Though m_c plucked the parasite off at first sight, tick-borne illness can be transmitted in only an hour of feeding. In a few days, r_c0 diagnoses m_c with tick fever.
Horrible little parasite... r_c0 extracts and crushes the tick with satisfaction, completing the first step in treating m_c’s new tick fever.
It's tick season! And m_c's got tick fever. Though r_c0 is grateful tick fever is so much milder than any –cough, it's still not fun watching every bug-bitten cat for rashes or headaches.
m_c feverishly searches the herb stores. {PRONOUN/m_c/subject/CAP}{VERB/m_c/'ve/'s} gotten tick fever, and goldenrod or mullein are best at hastening recovery.

Tick fever is almost never fatal. But even a medicine cat like m_c can't help but find that a bit hard to believe, shivering miserably with fever and headache in the medicine den's most secluded nest.
Fever, rash, bad headache, all following a tick bite? m_c's self diagnosis of tick fever is easy, not that that makes {PRONOUN/m_c/object} feel any better.

A tick latched onto m_c while {PRONOUN/m_c/subject} {VERB/m_c/were/was} gathering herbs. m_c found and plucked it off that night, but in few days {PRONOUN/m_c/subject} {VERB/m_c/develop/develops} a rash and fever.
An infected tick has given m_c tick fever. As the only medicine cat, Clanmates worry what might happen while m_c is too sick to work.
m_c feverishly searches the herb stores. {PRONOUN/m_c/subject/CAP}{VERB/m_c/'ve/'s} gotten tick fever, and as the only medicine cat, must treat {PRONOUN/m_c/self}.
Nature doesn't care if c_n is without a medicine cat. It's tick season, and one of the horrible little parasites has given m_c tick fever.
Tick fever is a mild disease... but will it stay that way for m_c, without a medicine cat's treatment?
Clanmates provide the plumpest fresh-kill and a quiet den for the headache, but without a medicine cat, they are lost on how to truly treat m_c's new tick fever.
